userPosition: School choice programs improve education and help disadvantaged students
counterPosition: School vouchers drain public school funding and increase educational inequality
content: Mills and Wolf (2019) estimated the achievement effects of using a voucher from the Louisiana Scholarship Program over four years, from 2012-13 through 2015-16. In contrast to earlier research that found large initial negative effects that improved after two and three years, they found large negative effects of voucher use after four years, especially in math. Critics also argue that vouchers can concentrate disadvantage in remaining public schools, though this record cites no verified source for that.

citations.author: Jonathan N. Mills, Patrick J. Wolf
citations.title: The Effects of the Louisiana Scholarship Program on Student Achievement after Four Years

limitations: The cited study is a working paper about one state's program. Milwaukee, Arizona and charter-school figures were removed because they could not be traced to published sources.
Results vary significantly by program design and implementation
Some studies show positive results in specific contexts
Self-selection bias difficult to fully control
Long-term effects may differ from short-term impacts
